summary: Canada’s restoration commitment is to plant 2 billion trees by 2031, backed by more than $3 billion over 10 years, and to restore wetlands, grasslands and other ecosystems; the tree count cannot be converted into a share of forest from the provided data. Conservation combines over $5 billion for natural climate solutions with 25% protection of both land and oceans by 2025 and 30% protection of each by 2030. The current landscape is 47.3% forest, 5.8% agriculture, 2.3% grassland and 0.8% wetland. Agricultural measures target 95% waste diversion, 12.5% of the S-CAP envelope for resilient agricultural landscapes, a 10–15% cut in Prince Edward Island agricultural emissions, and a 30% reduction in fertilizer-attributable emissions below 2020 levels by 2030. The forestry pillar targets 10–15% more carbon sequestration by 2030. These agricultural percentages do not denote coverage of the 576,442 km² agricultural area.
